We've got a set of ONNX tests currently xfailed (on several targets, cpu sync here):
```
FAILED iree-test-suites/onnx_ops/onnx/node/generated/test_dropout_default_mask_ratio/run_module_io_flags.txt::model.mlir::cpu_llvm_sync

FAILED iree-test-suites/onnx_ops/onnx/node/generated/test_split_zero_size_splits_opset18/run_module_io_flags.txt::model.mlir::cpu_llvm_sync
FAILED iree-test-suites/onnx_ops/onnx/node/generated/test_tril_zero/run_module_io_flags.txt::model.mlir::cpu_llvm_sync
FAILED iree-test-suites/onnx_ops/onnx/node/generated/test_triu_zero/run_module_io_flags.txt::model.mlir::cpu_llvm_sync
```

These result in segfaults on the bots that appear like the program winking out of existence with error code 245 (or others):
```
Stdout diagnostics:
EXEC @test_eyelike_without_dtype
<<empty>>

___ IREE compile and run: test_shape::model.mlir::model.mlir::cpu_llvm_sync ____
[gw0] linux -- Python 3.11.11 /home/runner/work/iree/iree/venv/bin/python
Error invoking iree-run-module
Error code: 245
Stderr diagnostics:
```

I forced on `--trace_execution` (`#define IREE_VM_EXECUTION_TRACING_FORCE_ENABLE 1` in `iree/base/config.h`) and every test fails at roughly the same point:
```
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype+00000000]    <block>
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype+00000001]    %r1 = vm.const.ref.zero
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype+00000004]    %i0 = vm.const.i32 -1  // 0xFFFFFFFF
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype+0000000B]    %i1 = vm.const.i32.zero
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype+0000000E]    %r2 = vm.call @hal.devices.get(%i1(0))
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype+0000001C]    %r2 = vm.call @hal.fence.create(%r2(!hal.device/0x0x4bdaee0), %i1(0))
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype+0000002C]    %r0 = vm.call @module.test_eyelike_without_dtype$async(%r0(!hal.buffer_view/0x0x4bdb420), %r1(null), %r2(!hal.fence/0x0x4bf25a0))
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype$async+00000000]    <block>
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype$async+00000001]    %i0 = vm.const.i32 268435[488](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/actions/runs/12934048267/job/36074593030?pr=19778#step:8:489)  // 0x10000020
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype$async+00000008]    %i1 = vm.const.i32 1  // 0x00000001
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype$async+0000000F]    %i2 = vm.const.i32 3075  // 0x00000C03
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype$async+00000016]    %i3 = vm.const.i32 48  // 0x00000030
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype$async+0000001D]    %i4 = vm.const.i32.zero
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype$async+00000020]    %i6:7 = vm.const.i64 4  // 0x0000000000000004
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype$async+0000002B]    %i8:9 = vm.const.i64.zero
[module.test_eyelike_without_dtype$async+0000002E]    %r0 = vm.const.ref.zero
iree_vm_ref_release 0x7ffc0f6daa08 2241944 0x4bdb420
```
(logs https://gist.githubusercontent.com/benvanik/050404176190bca8ef4b4103732bddd2/raw/dc37b60f978ce92193d7c244b0db1c5c1b70c7fc/gistfile1.txt)

The death happens somewhere within the iree_vm_ref_release but I have no stacks and no local repro to debug. What's happening here is the `vm.const.ref.zero` (NULL) is replacing the `%r0` register which already contains the `%arg0` buffer view of the function, the arg buffer view is being released (but _not_ destroyed, as the vm.list still contains a reference to it), and then it's dying before the next instruction is able to be printed. The commonality in these tests seems to be that the input argument is unused for some reason (entire thing const-evaled, the input wasn't needed for the non-const-eval work, etc).

Now the spooky: in the log above I added one printf in `iree_vm_ref_release` and it shows the valid pointer (the same passed in by the user). If I add _any_ other printf anywhere things start working with no segfaults. When I forced ASAN on (changing the `IREE_ENABLE_ASAN` cmake var to ON) even with no extra code things start working with no segfaults.

It's possible the release is not the issue but the next instruction in the bytecode but the disassembler should be dying when execution tracing is enabled and it's not. In all programs the subsequent operation is something like `%i12:13 = vm.const.i64 4` and not anything that would be expected to fail so I'm fairly certain it's somewhere between the call to release and the disassembly of the next op.

#19778 introduces a new `vm.call @hal.fence.await` op to initializers in some cases and it causes the failure to appear in new tests:
```
FAILED iree-test-suites/onnx_ops/onnx/node/generated/test_eyelike_populate_off_main_diagonal/run_module_io_flags.txt::model.mlir::cpu_llvm_sync
FAILED iree-test-suites/onnx_ops/onnx/node/generated/test_eyelike_with_dtype/run_module_io_flags.txt::model.mlir::cpu_llvm_sync
FAILED iree-test-suites/onnx_ops/onnx/node/generated/test_eyelike_without_dtype/run_module_io_flags.txt::model.mlir::cpu_llvm_sync
FAILED iree-test-suites/onnx_ops/onnx/node/generated/test_shape/run_module_io_flags.txt::model.mlir::cpu_llvm_sync
FAILED iree-test-suites/onnx_ops/onnx/node/generated/test_shape_clip_end/run_module_io_flags.txt::model.mlir::cpu_llvm_sync
FAILED iree-test-suites/onnx_ops/onnx/node/generated/test_shape_clip_start/run_module_io_flags.txt::model.mlir::cpu_llvm_sync
FAILED iree-test-suites/onnx_ops/onnx/node/generated/test_shape_end_negative_1/run_module_io_flags.txt::model.mlir::cpu_llvm_sync
FAILED iree-test-suites/onnx_ops/onnx/node/generated/test_shape_example/run_module_io_flags.txt::model.mlir::cpu_llvm_sync
FAILED iree-test-suites/onnx_ops/onnx/node/generated/test_shape_start_1/run_module_io_flags.txt::model.mlir::cpu_llvm_sync
```
This is spooky because the new op is in the initializer (which runs correctly) but the death still happens in the same place (in the subsequent function call by the application). In the case of local-sync (these tests) the fence wait is a no-op as nothing is asynchronous. The vulkan and rocm tests also fail, ruling out HAL implementations and codegen that may be corrupting memory.

Since ASAN hides the issue, printfs hide the issue, and I cannot reproduce this on windows or linux in any configuration (debug/release/asan/etc) I'm not sure how to make progress today besides xfailing the new set of tests that are dying. Until this is reproducible on any machine but the CI I have to chalk it up to something specific to that configuration (compiler/libraries/etc).

issue.body:
This allows for choosing whether initializers return immediately with asynchronous work still pending or if they block and wait prior to returning. Users benchmarking will want to use synchronous mode while users wanting to overlap other work with initialization will want asynchronous mode. Since all existing frameworks operate with synchronous initialization the default is changed to that.

For some spooky reason (#19795) this causes a few more onnx op tests to fail in addition to existing ones that were already failing. They've been xfailed for now because I cannot figure out what's going on or reproduce the issue.

Fixes #19770.

I am able to compile and benchmark with a local build of iree, however, using the same command with the iree-runtime python package exits and does not report anything when running `iree-run-module/iree-benchmark-module'.
